# OrderlyApp development guide — stabilization and product roadmap

Revision: 5 • Updated: 2026-10-11 • ST-02/ST-03 acceptance source: `a9537931c57cbf636466bf3f791e440e24ce74bd` on `fix/st02-st03-acceptance` • Release status: **Not completed**.

This is the single execution guide for taking the application to a stable **public mock demo**. ST-01 through ST-10 are implemented; ST-02/03 merged in PR47, ST-04/05/06 in PR48, and ST-07/08/09/10 in PR49. **ST-11 implementation/local acceptance and ST-12 repository/hosted CI acceptance are Completed and merged in PR50. The October 6 public acceptance candidate `c093125` passed seven CI gates and public receipt/isolation checks; current hosted staging operations use merged main `9a72d02`. Overall ST-13, INT-02 hosted staging and RELEASE-GATE remain Not completed.** Backend readiness and the public manual journey now pass after configuration repair: a fresh guest saves/reopens an exact receipt, and a second guest cannot read it. Isolated hosted restart/outage, backup/restore, retention and compatible rollback/current-main recovery now pass; actual cleanup scheduling and remaining hosted INT-02 cases are open. See [current criterion evidence](docs/qa/st11-st13-acceptance/results.md), [INT-01](docs/qa/int-01.md), [INT-02 local rehearsal](docs/qa/int-02.md) and [exact release identities/blockers](docs/releases/stabilization-acceptance.md). No public completion is inferred from local or CI results.

**Current direction — October 8:** The user deferred the remaining ST-13 checks and chose **history/reorder → discovery → voice**. The new plan is in [section17](#17-product-implementation-roadmap--history-discovery-voice); all new feature tickets are Not completed. The stabilization sections retain their scoped historical evidence. PR52 is merged and one manual production-configured cleanup run passed; scheduled-success/notification proof remains pending. This does not mark stabilization or the original release gate complete.

Think of the app as a shop made from Lego. The screens already look like a shop, but some connections behind them can lose a basket, show another visitor's receipt, or pretend an order succeeded when the server failed. First we strengthen those connections. Then we add more Lego.

## 0. Intern execution handbook

### 0.1 What to receive before starting one task

An implementation packet is the unit of work, not the entire 67-task restaurant release. The coordinator supplies: the selected packet; current `docs/repo_context.md`; current contents of every listed inspection file; the full COMMON rules and every consumed/produced contract, DTO and storage definition; synthetic fixture examples; the upstream source SHA; and the packet's verification commands. A contract ID alone is insufficient. For RS-01, copy the COMMON, DTO and proposed schema records from section18.6 into the owned contract document.

For a person with repository access, read these files directly. For a builder without repository tools, attach their contents. The coordinator includes the applicable security, API/database, frontend and testing rules in the packet rather than expecting an intern to find globally installed skills. Do not attach secrets, full `.env` files or production data.

Run intake before editing:

1. Check the dependency list against merged implementation and fixture evidence. `NOT FROZEN`, an absent CREATE file, or a proposed shape is not a usable runtime provider.
   Consumer test/UI preparation may start from a frozen fixture where the DAG permits parallel start. That does not satisfy the separate provider merge/runtime gate. Record which kind of readiness you have.
2. Identify the exact owned files. CREATE means create only if absent; if a previous task already created it, continue the actual file after receiving its handoff. Never overwrite existing work from a template.
3. Match the contract example to the actual provider output. A mismatch goes to the architect with the contract ID, expected field, observed field and source SHA. Do not guess a new schema, tax rate, role, provider setting or retry rule.
4. Record which work is synthetic and which needs U1–U4 evidence. Synthetic implementation may proceed where the packet permits it; real activation stays blocked. No intern is expected to obtain policy or account approvals by improvising.
5. Choose the narrow test command in the packet and confirm its test file exists or belongs to the owned CREATE list. Missing ownership of an essential fixture/test is a packet correction, not permission to edit unrelated files.

Specific named contract rules take precedence over repeated generic prose within the same packet. For example, an explicitly documented 404, body-size rejection, webhook signature rejection or uncertain response must not be replaced with a generic 422/503 sentence. If two specific contracts disagree, stop that boundary and return a Contract Change Record request.

### 0.2 Establish a reproducible local baseline

Run commands from the repository root unless a command explicitly changes directory. These commands were checked against source on October11,2026; their presence is not a passing runtime result. Supported CI uses Node22, npm11.20.0, Python3.12, PostgreSQL16 and Redis7. Use `package-lock.json` and `backend/requirements-test.lock`; do not update dependencies merely to install the project.

```sh
pwd
git status --short
git branch --show-current
git rev-parse HEAD
node --version
npm --version
python3 --version
```

Save the source SHA and the initial dirty-file list in a private working note. Preserve other people's edits. The selected packet determines work; a dirty checkout does not authorize reset, stash, checkout, commits or publication. Branch/issue/PR details are discovered when publication is requested; this documentation change creates none.

Install only when the environment is not already prepared:

```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
python3 -m venv /private/tmp/orderly-guide-venv
. /private/tmp/orderly-guide-venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e ./backend
python -m pip install -r backend/requirements-test.lock
```

Use a fresh venv path if that directory already belongs to another session. The activation line must run in each new terminal used for Python. A missing module error is an installation/interpreter failure, not an application-test result. `npm run lint` now runs genuine ESLint, as `package.json` confirms; section2's older typecheck-only observation is historical.

### 0.3 Use disposable services for database and browser verification

The existing Compose file persists named volumes and uses port3100 for web. Do not assume it is an empty test database. Playwright defaults to port3200. Pick one origin consistently across `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` and the backend allowed origins. Do not mix `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` for guest-cookie tests.

If Docker is available and these container names/ports are free, the following is a disposable test arrangement. The `orderly` password below is a synthetic local-container value. Never substitute a production connection string:

```sh
docker ps --format '{{.Names}} {{.Ports}}'
docker run --rm --name orderly-guide-postgres -e POSTGRES_DB=orderlyapp_test -e POSTGRES_USER=orderly -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=orderly -p 127.0.0.1:55432:5432 -d postgres:16-alpine
docker run --rm --name orderly-guide-redis -p 127.0.0.1:56379:6379 -d redis:7-alpine
export DATABASE_URL='postgresql://orderly:orderly@127.0.0.1:55432/orderlyapp_test'
export ORDERLY_TEST_DATABASE_URL="$DATABASE_URL"
export REDIS_URL='redis://127.0.0.1:56379'
docker exec orderly-guide-postgres pg_isready -U orderly -d orderlyapp_test
docker exec orderly-guide-redis redis-cli ping
```

Proceed only after PostgreSQL says it accepts connections and Redis returns PONG. If either name/port is occupied, inspect it and select a different private test arrangement; do not stop someone else's container. Export the same variables in each test/API terminal. The current pytest fixture can fall back to `DATABASE_URL` and skips locally when neither URL is set; therefore an exit0 with skipped PostgreSQL cases does not satisfy a storage ticket.

For baseline API/browser tests, set the following in both API and web/test terminals. The secret is explicitly a disposable test secret, not a deployable credential:

```sh
export ORDERLY_ENVIRONMENT=test
export ORDERLY_DATA_MODE=api
export NEXT_PUBLIC_ORDERLY_DATA_MODE=api
export ORDERLY_SOURCE_SHA="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
export ORDERLY_SESSION_SECRET='disposable-guide-session-secret-not-for-deployment'
export ORDERLY_ALLOWED_ORIGINS='http://127.0.0.1:3200'
export ORDERLY_CORS_ORIGINS='http://127.0.0.1:3200'
export ORDERLY_API_ORIGIN='http://127.0.0.1:8000'
export NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL='http://127.0.0.1:8000'
export NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL='http://127.0.0.1:3200'
export PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL='http://127.0.0.1:3200'
export NEXT_PUBLIC_VOICE_MODE=mock
export NEXT_PUBLIC_CHECKOUT_MODE=mock
export NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_PROVIDER=none
python backend/scripts/migrate.py
ORDERLY_ALLOW_FIXTURE_SEED=1 python backend/scripts/seed_postgres.py
```

Seeding is allowed only on the disposable fixture database above. It is not live tenant provisioning; RS-67 creates that separately. Start FastAPI in a separate activated terminal, leaving the process running:

```sh
cd backend
uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
```

In the root test terminal:

```sh
curl --fail --silent http://127.0.0.1:8000/health/ready
npm run test:e2e:install
npm run test:e2e:list
npx playwright test --grep-invert 'local_demo'
```

Readiness must report the intended source, API mode and healthy schema/database. Listing tests proves discovery only. Playwright starts Next on3200 unless `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_WEBSERVER=1`; inspect any already-running server because configuration permits reuse locally. Installed Chromium, a launched browser and passing product assertions are separate checks. New live routes are absent until their providers are implemented; these baseline commands alone cannot accept them. RS-62 supplies synthetic staff/provider fixtures under a production-denied test setup, not real JWT bypasses or provider credentials.

For fixture preview, use a separate web/test terminal with both data modes `local_demo`, then `npx playwright test --grep 'local_demo'`. Stop the prior owned web process before reusing3200; never interpret a reused API-mode server as preview proof. Stop only these disposable containers when finished, after saving sanitized evidence. They use no named database volume, so stopping them discards their synthetic records.

### 0.4 Complete one small verified change at a time

Use the packet's ordered implementation steps plus its worked verification below. For each step write a short private record: step ID, objective, owned files, prerequisite, expected result, check/result and documentation impact. Start with the failing behavior test when practical; change the shared owner once; run the packet's narrow command; review the diff. Keep behavior and its essential tests together. A checkpoint approximately every five meaningful changes reviews cumulative scope and contract compatibility. Do not manufacture50 checklist items or50 commits for a small packet; the remaining real work determines the count.

When publication is separately authorized, reuse the actual main issue/branch/PR and make coherent micro-commits referencing the packet/step IDs. Until then, local documentation and implementation evidence do not imply an issue, commit, push or merge. A checked guide step requires its stated proof even if no tracker exists.

### 0.5 Worked scenarios, evidence and handoff

Every implementation packet below has a **Worked verification for a new implementer** block. Its values are synthetic test vectors, not replacement production defaults. Put each named scenario in an owned test file; use deterministic IDs/time and the packet's actual field names. For private boundaries, prepare two restaurants, two guests and an owner/order_staff/cashier membership set where needed. Use stable valid UUIDs for UUID fields; `r-demo` and `r-other` are TEXT restaurant IDs. Never use a QR/table identifier as authorization.

For a side-effect test, assert both the visible response and the durable result: count rows/events/command records and compare before/after state. For a denied action, assert zero business writes and zero provider calls. For a race, coordinate two independent connections with a barrier or blocking test hook; do not hope a timed sleep creates concurrency. Failures are injected in test transports/transactions, never by interrupting production. A money test asserts exact integers; a callback test verifies the original raw body; a browser test asserts state and requests, not just a screenshot.

Save this record through the packet's existing evidence owner/path. If no artifact is owned, send it to the integration owner; do not create arbitrary checked-in logs:

```text
Task / criterion / scenario:
Source SHA / dirty diff identifier / upstream contract version:
Environment / synthetic fixture IDs / runtime versions:
Prerequisites actually met:
Command or manual action:
Expected response and durable state:
Observed response and durable state:
PASS | FAIL | BLOCKED | NOT RUN:
Evidence path / test name / timestamp with timezone:
Changed files / documentation delta / recovery action:
Consumer now unlocked, or exact remaining blocker:
```

Redact tokens, cookies, credentials, destinations, transcripts and message text. A successful command with no matching tests, a skipped database test, a fake microphone, or HTTP202 from a messaging provider is not evidence for the corresponding real behavior. An unimplemented worked scenario stays NOT RUN; adding these instructions does not alter historical ticket status.

Before handing off, the coordinator compares provider output to the copied contract, refreshes affected fixtures/source attachments, runs the consumer conformance check and records the freeze SHA. The intern returns only owned changes, exact checks/results, remaining decisions and the documentation delta. The coordinator updates shared guide/context/status files and named downstream consumers. No ordinary implementation choice may be hidden behind “ask whoever built the previous task.”

### 0.6 Diagnose failures without weakening the checks

| Symptom | First check | Required next action |
|---|---|---|
| `No tests found`, zero selected tests or missing CREATE path | Confirm packet path, working directory and provider/task completion | Create only the owned missing test or return the packet to its owner; do not add `--passWithNoTests` |
| PostgreSQL tests show `skipped` | Check activated interpreter and explicit disposable test URL in this terminal | Provision the test service and rerun; skipped assertions stay NOT RUN, even if exit status is0 |
| API readiness fails | Compare mode, schema, allowed origins, secret presence and source identity; inspect safe reason codes | Fix the test configuration/migration before browser checks; do not seed an unknown DB or force a200 |
| Guest action denied/receipt disappears in another tab | Compare exact origin, active cookie scope, reset/expiry and owner-qualified lookup | Restore a valid test session or verify intended isolation; do not use localStorage IDs to bypass authorization |
| Cart/config409 | Compare reviewed revision/version with returned current state | Preserve draft and require review; no automatic overwrite/revision bump |
| Mutation timeout,5xx or malformed success | Inspect saved command identity/body and accepted durable state through the contracted recovery path | Keep outcome uncertain and reconcile original identity; never clear recovery or retry with a new key to make UI proceed |
| Queue shows empty after network failure | Distinguish successful empty response from unavailable/stale state | Keep stale warning and mutations disabled; fix failed read, not an empty fixture fallback |
| Provider202 or returned message ID | Check accepted versus authenticated delivered evidence | Record accepted only; no resend or delivered claim from transport acceptance |
| Microphone mock passes, real browser fails | Record support, HTTPS, permission, device and locale | Retain editable text fallback and mark real-device criterion separately; do not fabricate speech |
| Test expects a contract field the implementation lacks | Compare copied contract, fixture version and provider SHA | Return exact drift to architect/provider; update affected contracts/fixtures/consumers together |

For a reproducible defect, supply the smallest synthetic input, exact route/action, expected/actual status and state, owning task, test name and source SHA. Keep secrets out of that report. Fixes belong to the provider/consumer that owns the failed boundary, not the QA checkpoint's product-source diff.

## 1. Project charter

**Goal:** A visitor can browse an authoritative restaurant menu, customize an item, edit a basket, select a demo delivery address, submit mock checkout once, and reopen the same complete receipt. Reloads, retries, another browser tab and temporary server failures must not corrupt this journey.

**Confirmed user decisions:** Stabilize before adding features; target a public mock demo; use password-free demo profiles; postpone voice until stabilization. The original documentation task requested **no coding**; subsequent explicit requests authorize ticket implementation and microcommit publication.

**Scope:** Existing manual ordering, demo profile/address screens, scoped guest data, canonical pricing, cart persistence, honest error states, receipt/history correctness, safe startup, reproducible checks and verified public access. The mock payment screen must collect no real card information. A stored order means “mock order saved,” not a restaurant accepted it or a driver is coming.

**Mode boundary:** The public release uses `api`. `local_demo` is a development/test fixture preview limited to browsing, customization and a namespaced local basket. It shows a persistent “Local fixture preview — checkout unavailable” label, needs no guest session/backend, and disables checkout, receipt and history routes with an explanatory state. It creates no orders and promises no server persistence or guest isolation. It is not an alternative public release or an outage fallback. ST-08 owns these restrictions; ST-09 verifies direct checkout/receipt/history navigation cannot bypass them.

**Non-goals:** Real payments/refunds, restaurant onboarding, drivers, dispatch, real accounts/OAuth, email/SMS, LLMs, speech/microphone UI, new cuisines, loyalty, recommendations and administrator dashboards. These need later charters. Existing voice/parser code can remain unused; it must not be promoted as a working feature.

**Success measures:** All release-gate cases pass on one identified candidate; separate visitors cannot access each other's data; backend faults never create pretend API success; receipt totals and address survive refresh; one checkout key produces one durable order; restarting the backend preserves data/catalog; the public URL can be opened without developer sign-in. No arbitrary conversion, traffic or latency claims are made.

**Authority:** These are local Markdown tickets. Future coding, tracker publication and deployment are separate operations. Keep unrelated audit/graph files and user changes intact. Implementation owner is unassigned; no new thread is implied.

Evidence baseline is the October 4 audit, not a new runtime test performed while saving this document. See [assessment](docs/audit-2026-10-04/ASSESSMENT.md), [verification record](docs/audit-2026-10-04/verification.json), [QA charters](docs/audit-2026-10-04/qa-charters.md) and [repository context](docs/repo_context.md). The older [implementation proposal](docs/audit-2026-10-04/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md) included an assistant; this guide supersedes that scope and its pending audience/account decisions.

| `app/page.tsx`, `app/restaurants/page.tsx`, menu/item pages; `lib/marketplace.ts`, `lib/mock-data.ts` | Discovery and customization use local catalog fixtures despite API helpers | API-mode screens use canonical catalog; fixtures only in explicit local demo |
| `lib/api.ts`: `fetchRestaurants`, `fetchRestaurant`, `fetchCart`, `saveCart`, `createBackendOrder`, `fetchOrder`, `fetchOrders` | Different failures collapse to undefined/false; session IDs come from browser storage | Typed errors, server guest ownership, consistent same-origin transport |

Frontend baseline: Next 16.2.2, React 19.2.4, TypeScript, Vitest and Playwright. Backend: FastAPI/Pydantic with Postgres, Redis and JSON paths. ## 3. Architecture Decision Register

“Locked for this plan” describes design direction, not implemented or tested code. New evidence requiring a change must update this guide, schemas, fixtures and consumers before implementation continues.

| ID | Status / choice | Why / rejected alternative / consequence | Contracts |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADR-01 | User-confirmed: public mock demo, manual flow first | A real service adds payment/provider/operations obligations. Voice waits outside this DAG | All |
| ADR-02 | User-confirmed: password-free demo profiles; technical choice: server guest identity | A profile name is a label, not authentication. Changing it never grants another visitor's orders | C1, C2 |
| ADR-03 | Locked: Next same-origin `/api/orderly` gateway; FastAPI validates a signed HttpOnly guest cookie | Avoid direct browser ownership IDs and cross-site cookie complexity. Proxy does not trust browser-supplied internal headers | C1 |
| ADR-04 | Locked: Postgres authoritative in API mode; no Redis authority or JSON failover | Three writable copies cannot reliably agree. Redis is unused for correctness; local_demo remains explicitly local | C3, C4, C5 |
| ADR-05 | Locked: revision compare-and-swap carts and immutable receipts | A second tab must not silently overwrite a newer basket; menu edits must not change old receipts | C4, C5 |
| ADR-06 | Locked: owner-scoped idempotency, transaction includes order + cart clear | Browser disabling alone cannot prevent duplicate requests or recover lost responses | C6 |
| ADR-07 | Locked: public release uses `api`; explicit `local_demo` is development/test browsing and basket preview only | A server outage is an error, not permission to invent an accepted order; preview has no checkout/receipts/history | C0, C7 |
| ADR-08 | Locked: additive migrations, one deploy migration job, explicit fixture seed | Boot reseeding erases catalog edits. Preserve legacy records without claiming their ownership | C4–C6, C8 |
| ADR-09 | Locked: integer cents; round half up; server quote and snapshot | Python/JS rounding can differ. Promo is server policy, never a submitted discount amount | C3, C5 |
| ADR-10 | Locked: mock order remains `Placed`; no time-driven delivery claim | “Placed” is durable mock storage, not restaurant acknowledgement. Simulator features need later scope | C5, C7 |
| ADR-11 | Locked: 30-day guest session/data window, explicit forget/reset, no cross-device recovery | Anonymous cookies cannot securely recover lost identity. Use synthetic address/contact fixtures; expired guests receive new isolated scope | C1, C2, C8 |

## 4. System invariants

| ID | Always-true rule, in plain words | Enforcement | Proof owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| INV-01 | Your basket and receipts belong only to your browser guest | Verified cookie owner on every protected query | ST-02, INT-01 |
| INV-02 | Server failure never means an API order succeeded | Explicit mode and typed results | ST-09, INT-01 |
| INV-03 | Old receipts stay exactly as saved | Snapshot fields, no catalog reconstruction | ST-06, ST-09 |
| INV-04 | Retrying the same checkout creates at most one order | Owner/key unique constraint and atomic transaction | ST-07 |
| INV-05 | A basket contains valid items from one restaurant | Canonical validation, limits, availability | ST-04, ST-05 |
| INV-06 | An old tab cannot silently erase newer edits | Revision comparison; conflict preserves current state | ST-05, ST-08 |
| INV-07 | API data has one durable source | Postgres-only authority; required faults fail safely | ST-05, ST-11 |
| INV-08 | Names, prices and money are determined by server rules | Reject injected price/name/discount authority | ST-04, ST-06 |
| INV-09 | Demo profiles collect no passwords or real payment details | Remove credential UI/storage; mock payment only | ST-03, ST-10 |
| INV-10 | Restarting does not replace catalog or lose accepted receipts | Separate seed/migration; durability checks | ST-11, INT-02 |
| INV-11 | A displayed order is the exact requested order | Owner-scoped ID lookup; no latest-order fallback | ST-09 |
| INV-12 | Completion claims refer to evidence for a named build | Evidence ledger and release checklist | ST-12, ST-13 |

## 6. Contract registry

A contract is a promise between two parts of the program. For example: “give me a valid basket revision and I either save the whole change or explain why I rejected it.” A consumer should need this promise and examples, not private database implementation details.

The contract designs below remain authoritative. **C0 is frozen by completed ST-01 at schema version 1. C1/C2 version-1 local provider/consumer conformance is frozen for candidate `a9537931c57cbf636466bf3f791e440e24ce74bd`; hosted CI/merge remain pending. C3–C8 release status is not reconciled by this scoped follow-up.** One source-of-truth owner is named for each contract; after the ST-01 scaffold handoff, the provider owns changes.

**Shared HTTP rules:** JSON envelope has `schema_version: 1`. Browser API base is `/api/orderly`; the gateway forwards versioned backend routes under `/v1`. Protected routes use the verified guest cookie, never a request `session_id` or `owner_id`. Error response is `{ "error": { "code": "cart_conflict", "message": "Basket changed in another tab", "request_id": "synthetic-request-1", "fields": [] } }`, with optional `current_cart` on cart conflicts. No tracebacks, tokens or DB URLs are returned. Reject unknown write fields. Limit request body to 64 KiB; notes 500 chars, address instructions 500 chars; max 50 lines, quantities 1–10, no duplicate group/option IDs. Strict money integers; invalid floats/negative amounts are rejected. Same-origin unsafe requests require exact allowed Origin; proxy forwards cookies and Set-Cookie safely, strips spoofable internal identity headers and never redirects to arbitrary targets.

**Common contract change protocol:** Provider proposes a versioned change here, updates every listed consumer and fixture, reruns conformance and affected integration gates, and freezes again. Additive optional fields may stay v1; changed required fields/semantics require v2 or a coordinated maintenance deployment. No mixed old browser/client assumptions silently fall back. Read-only legacy records remain preserved but inaccessible through unowned public endpoints.

### C5 pricing and checkout details — exact rules

For `mock-v1`: line unit = canonical item price + selected option deltas; subtotal = sum(unit × quantity). Recognized optional promo `DEMO5` discounts min(500, subtotal); no other code is accepted. Delivery fee = restaurant delivery fee for a nonempty cart; service fee =249 cents for a nonempty cart. Tax = round-half-up((subtotal−discount)×875/10000), implemented with integer arithmetic. Tip is integer0–10000 cents; total = subtotal−discount+delivery+service+tax+tip. Empty quote is rejected for checkout. These are mock policy numbers, not real tax/legal claims. UI must show code/fee policy explicitly rather than silently granting a discount. The above fixture produces 1192 cents. A taxable 40 cents yields tax4 cents, exercising half-up rather than Python bankers rounding.

Checkout fields: name1–100 chars, synthetic phone1–30, email valid shape≤254, street1–200, apartment≤50, city1–100, state2 uppercase letters, postal_code five digits or five+four, delivery_instructions≤500, payment_method exactly `mock`. The public demo offers supplied synthetic contact/address choices and warns against real personal data; no address provider or real deliverability promise. Receipt includes every field selected, canonical item/modifier labels, unit/line prices, all totals, timestamp and pricing version. Fingerprint changes invalidate quote; no automatic higher-price submission. The client must show new quote and obtain another deliberate submit.

**C6 persistence fields:** Guest table: UUID owner, created_at, expires_at, revoked_at. Cart: owner PK/FK, revision bigint, canonical items JSONB, updated_at. Orders: UUID id, owner FK, immutable snapshot JSONB, created_at. Idempotency: owner+key unique, canonical payload SHA256, order_id FK. Cart line ID is a bounded unique string inside its basket. Legacy existing tables are retained/read-isolated during cutover; do not infer owner from mutable browser/session IDs. Backend schema migrations add guest tables/columns without destructive conversion.

### ST-05 — Persist baskets with revisions and no hidden failover

**Status:** Completed — merged PR #48; local acceptance verified; hosted release gates separate. **Execution owner:** Codex. See [criterion evidence](docs/qa/st04-st06-acceptance/acceptance.md). **Objective:** Two writes with one expected revision yield one success and one409; no silent overwrite.

## 13. Critical path and parallelization

Core path: ST-01 → ST-02 → ST-04 → ST-05 → ST-06 → ST-07 → ST-09 → INT-01 → ST-10 → INT-02 → ST-13 → RELEASE-GATE. Operational convergence: ST-07 → ST-11 → ST-12 → INT-02. The slower convergence controls release. ST-03 can run with ST-04; ST-08 with ST-06; ST-11 with ST-09; ST-12 with ST-10 once shared writers have finished. These are bounded possibilities, not permission to spawn workers.

Shared main/models/store writes are serialized through backend waves. `lib/types.ts` moves from ST-03 to ST-08 to ST-09; account/profile code moves ST-03 to ST-10. Locks/test-runner config moves ST-01 to ST-12. Baseline CI starts in ST-01; behavior owners serialize additions to their test jobs before ST-12 completes the release matrix. Provider contract fixture ownership moves from ST-01 to the named provider. If a dependency update requires source fixes, assign them back to the owning ticket and retest, rather than allowing CI ticket to secretly rewrite the app.

Summed implementation estimates are 35 engineer-days; integration/release verification adds2.5 days. These are planning estimates, not a promised calendar date. Infrastructure access, discoveries and fix/retest cycles can change them. Adding developers does not remove transaction/contract/shared-file dependencies. The first useful vertical slice ends at INT-01; do not wait for live release to discover basic basket/checkout mismatches.

## 15. Risks and true blockers

**Current execution prerequisites, not unanswered product design:** ST-01 has now verified isolated PostgreSQL, browser runtime, workflow publication, and hosted CI execution. ST-11 still requires its own isolation proof, and later release work still requires deployment read access. Public deployment configuration/credentials and existing platform aggregate rate limiting must be verified before exposing checkout; if unavailable, keep public checkout disabled until the supported mechanism is configured. No spending or infrastructure purchase is authorized here.

**Data compatibility risk:** Legacy carts/orders have insufficient verified ownership and incomplete receipt fields. Preserve them offline and explicitly classify legacy data; do not migrate guesses into a new guest. For a demo this is a defensible reset of reachable data, but backups still matter.

**Anonymous identity tradeoff:** Losing cookie/signing secret loses access to prior scoped demo history. This is explicit behavior, not a bug repaired by trusting an email/profile label. Real account recovery is later work.

**Scope drift risk:** Voice/AI, real payments and real restaurant status look attractive before the foundations work. They are excluded from stabilization and cannot be slipped into acceptance tickets. local_demo is a development/test fixture preview, not a second complete ordering implementation. After RELEASE-GATE, a separate backlog may evaluate deterministic typed assistant, accessible speech input, real identity, payment sandbox/provider integration and operator tooling, each with new evidence and product decisions.

**Evidence drift risk:** Framework advisories and deployment URLs change. Refresh when implementing/releasing. Historical 37 passing tests, earlier tracker Done labels and successful deploy state do not prove this candidate is stable.

No additional user product decision blocks this document: audience, profiles and voice timing were answered. Technical choices are recorded above. Authorization for coding/deployment/tracker writes remains outside this documentation request.

## 17. Product implementation roadmap — history, discovery, voice

**Plan date:** 2026-10-08. **User-confirmed sequence:** (1) order history and reorder, (2) restaurant discovery, (3) voice ordering. **Authority:** planning and saving this guide only; this request does not implement features, create tracker issues, commit, push, merge, deploy, provision providers, or incur charges. All feature tickets below are **Not completed / queued**. Ownership: the future implementer in this repository; the plan creates no new chat or delegated worker.

**Stabilization handoff:** On October 8 the user explicitly chose to move on from ST-13. Its remaining checks, INT-02 and the original release gate stay **Not completed / deferred by user**, not passed or waived. PR52 is merged. The [manual cleanup run](https://github.com/anmolsansi/OrderlyApp/actions/runs/37792941487) succeeded on `f1ab73f3eca6fa9d3bf297358c0efd85c594bfd8`, reporting `deleted=0`. This proves one successful manual invocation; successful scheduled execution and failure-notification verification remain pending. The secret value and production database identity were not inspected. Feature acceptance below does not certify the deferred stabilization release gate.

**In plain words:** History is your old shopping receipt. Reorder turns that receipt into a new shopping list, checks today's menu, and asks before changing your basket. Discovery helps you find the right shop and dish. Voice converts a sentence into a proposed shopping-list change; you check it before it touches the basket. None of these buttons sends an order to a real restaurant.

### 17.1 Project charter

**Goal and audience:** Help visitors to this public pizza mock demo repeat a previous order, find restaurants and dishes more easily, and use short spoken commands while preserving the manual ordering path. A visitor owns data through the current browser's signed guest cookie. A display profile is not a real account.

**Current → desired:** History already lists up to 50 receipts and opens the exact saved receipt; add page loading and a reviewed reorder action. Discovery already has search, one filter and sort; make combined filters, URLs and menu search consistent. An unused voice parser exists; replace fixture-first guesses with catalog-grounded proposals, add explicit microphone control, and reuse the reviewed cart action.

**Success measures:** All numbered feature criteria pass on a named source/build; old receipt bytes stay unchanged; basket changes appear only after server acceptance; cancellation causes zero writes; changed or missing catalog choices are visible; history is isolated by guest; discovery survives reload/back/forward; speech cannot silently choose a restaurant or place checkout. Real microphone support is accepted only after a human exercises it on HTTPS. No invented conversion or latency targets.

**Scope:** Current pizza catalog, guest history, reorder with current prices, one-restaurant baskets, multiple discovery filters, deterministic sorting, menu search, English short voice commands, explicit review, supported-browser microphone use, and typed fallback. Existing mock checkout remains the only order-submission path.

**Non-goals:** Real payments/accounts, login synchronization, permanent or cross-device history, restaurant onboarding, new cuisines/data feeds, geographic routing, true pickup, delivery tracking, recommendations/embeddings, search services, loyalty, real-time agents, always-listening microphones, recorded audio storage, external speech/LLM providers, voice checkout, and multi-item conversational ordering in one utterance. These require separately agreed scope. The stabilization chapter's voice exclusion applies to that earlier phase; this chapter authorizes planning voice as Phase 3.

**Working assumptions:** First voice version uses browser recognition plus editable text, `en-US`, one command at a time, on the selected restaurant's menu. A question about an external AI speech service was presented; no provider choice or spending is inferred from silence. Browser recognition is the reversible planning default. If the user selects external AI, revise VO-02/VO-03 and their privacy/cost contracts before implementing them; Phase 1 and Phase 2 are unaffected.

**Completion rule:** Queued → implementing → ready for QA → fixes requested or verified. A feature checkpoint is accepted only with exact-build evidence. Local unit success, CI success, publication, deployment, hosted acceptance, and human microphone acceptance are separate fields. No source changes are authorized by this plan request.

### 17.3 Architecture Decision Register

“Locked” is a technical plan, not evidence of implemented behavior. Product assumptions are labeled separately.

| ID / status | Decision and reason | Alternative rejected / consequence | Contracts / owners |
|---|---|---|---|
| FADR-01 Locked | Extend existing history/API instead of building a second order model. | No new orders table or summary endpoint; historic prices stay saved. | FH / OH-01 |
| FADR-02 Locked | Reorder means review then replace full basket using one existing revisioned PUT. | No automatic merge or clear-then-add loop; existing basket requires explicit replacement even for the same restaurant. | FP, FA / OH-02, OH-03 |
| FADR-03 Locked | Resolve old IDs against today's fetched catalog; invalid/missing choices block application. | Never choose replacement dish/modifier silently. User can browse/customize manually. All-or-nothing first version; partial reorder deferred. | FP / OH-02 |
| FADR-04 Locked | Draft uses fresh stable-for-this-attempt line IDs and current prices; server accepted cart remains authority. | No old receipt line IDs, client-trusted money or reused old checkout. Draft shows estimated item subtotal; final fees/tax/tip only at checkout. | FP, FA |
| FADR-05 Locked | Use one pure frontend discovery helper over selected catalog, with URL-owned combined filters. | No new search service/backend search contract, autocomplete or caches. Browser work is linear in current catalog size. Reassess if catalog growth is measured. | FD / DS-01 |
| FADR-06 Locked | Remove misleading Pickup control/normalize old pickup URLs to delivery. Existing sort/time/distance are demo catalog metadata. | No pickup ordering or location claims; no schema changes. | FD / DS-02 |
| FADR-07 Locked | Share one reviewed cart proposal flow between reorder and voice because both need the same accepted-cart/conflict behavior. | No new command bus, state framework or second cart store. | FA / OH-03, VO-03 |
| FADR-08 Locked | Voice parser is a pure function taking supplied selected Restaurant; IDs come only from that catalog; ambiguity yields choices. | No fixture import, first-result guess, fuzzy/LLM confidence threshold or unreviewed write. | FV / VO-01 |
| FADR-09 Working assumption | Browser SpeechRecognition, explicit Start/Stop/Cancel, typed fallback, en-US; no app-paid provider. | Browser support/recognition service is outside app control; no offline or wholly-local privacy promise. External provider requires replanning. | FS / VO-02 |
| FADR-10 Locked | Voice initial command grammar: add one configured item/quantity, show cart, remove a specified line, clear cart. Never order submission. | “Order pizza” means draft item request only if resolvable; “place/pay/confirm order” cannot call checkout. Multiple items in one phrase ask one-at-a-time. | FV, FA / VO-01, VO-03 |
| FADR-11 Locked | Release phases in the requested order; each checkpoint consumes its real integrated journey. | Later work does not retroactively claim stabilization complete. No paid resources or deployment in planning. | FG1–FG3 |
| FADR-12 Locked | No new DB schema, backend API, provider credentials or Redis authority. | Current retention/expiry persists; guest reset loses access to old history. | all |

| ID | Property | Enforcement / owner | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| FINV-01 | Guest data belongs only to current signed guest; UI profile cannot grant ownership. | Existing API + OH-01/OH-03 | foreign receipt/cursor, forged profile, reset/session tests |
| FINV-02 | Old receipts never change after reorder, catalog edit or voice. | immutable snapshots + OH-02 | before/after full receipt comparison |
| FINV-03 | User cancel/review/transcription has no cart or order write. | reviewed action + VO-01/OH-03 | count mutation requests; compare cart revision |
| FINV-04 | Every proposed choice is valid in current catalog; no guessed alternatives. | OH-02/VO-01 + existing canonical validator | missing option/item, required choice, duplicate names, unrelated fixture |
| FINV-05 | Only accepted server basket appears as saved; concurrent/retry errors do not silently overwrite. | FA + revisioned PUT | double-click, lost response, shared tabs, stale revision |
| FINV-06 | One restaurant, ≤50 lines, quantity integer 1–10, integer cents. | existing catalog + draft/parser | boundary and mixed-restaurant tests |
| FINV-07 | Only existing manual checkout creates an order; existing recovery/key is preserved. | FA/VO-03 | assert no orders POST from proposal; uncertain checkout blocks mutation |
| FINV-08 | API outage never activates fixture data; preview never has history/reorder/API voice writes. | adapter + all UI owners | API503 and local_demo zero-request tests |
| FINV-09 | URL and shown discovery state agree across refresh/back/forward; results deterministic. | FD/DS-02/DS-03 | property/boundary + browser URL tests |
| FINV-10 | Microphone starts only from deliberate action and stops on cancel/end/navigation; late events ignored. | FS/VO-02 | fake recognizer lifecycle + human HTTPS check |
| FINV-11 | New features retain no audio/transcript/credentials and copy no historic address into drafts; existing receipt/checkout storage keeps its established contract. No private content in telemetry. | VO-02/VO-03 + all packet owners | storage/log/network inspection with synthetic canaries |
| FINV-12 | Completed means exact-build accepted; feature verification never changes deferred ST-13 to pass. | G1–G3 + coordinator | criterion evidence and status reconciliation |

### 17.6 Contract registry

Every contract version is **feature-v1**; existing receipt/cart schemaVersion remains **1**. Freeze means provider tests plus synthetic consumer fixture are committed and passing, not this proposed document alone. After freeze: list every consumer, change shape/errors/fixtures here, update consumer packets, run conformance tests, then land consumers together. No silent breaking change. Common adapter failures are typed `ApiResult`: validation, conflict, session, network, server; browser must not collapse them to empty success. New client-only codes below are proposal issues, not new HTTP statuses.

#### FH — Guest history pages

- **Provider / source / type:** existing `backend/app/main.py:orders_index`, `store.py:list_order_snapshots_for_owner`, `lib/api.ts:fetchOrderReceipts`; OH-01 owns browser consumption. API read contract; consumers OH-03, G1.
- **Inputs:** signed current guest; `{limit:20,cursor?:lastOwnedReceiptId,signal?}`. Backend supports limit1–50. First page omits cursor; never send profile ID.
- **Outputs:** existing `ApiResult<OrderReceipt[]>`; full immutable receipts, descending createdAt then id. Receipt names/prices reflect saved snapshot. No saved restaurant-name field. IDs are UUID strings; last row ID is next cursor.
- **Pre/post:** API mode; initialized verified guest. OH-01 may CREATE `lib/history.ts:mergeReceiptPage` and `nextReceiptCursor` for pure pagination state checks. Read does not mutate cart/order. Empty page means no next results, not an API fault. A full page may expose Load more; final exact-size page can require one final empty request.
- **Errors / retry:** invalid/foreign cursor uses existing `invalid_receipt_cursor` typed validation; refresh first page deliberately. Network/503 shows retry while retaining already-loaded rows. Session reset discards displayed old rows rather than refetching under old ownership.
- **Ordering / concurrency / security:** dedupe pages by ID, retain server order; one in-flight page; AbortSignal and generation guard ignore late responses. New order arrivals appear on explicit refresh, not by corrupting an old cursor.
- **Compatibility / fixture / freeze:** existing array response unchanged. **CREATE** `tests/fixtures/features/history.json` by OH-01: 20+1 records, tie timestamp, empty, foreign cursor, error. Freeze at OH-01 unit/API conformance pass.
- **Verification:** adapter query tests, owned/foreign cursor backend regression, >20-order browser journey, G1. No history in local_demo.

#### FP — Reorder proposal from an immutable receipt

- **Provider / source / type:** OH-02; **CREATE** `lib/reorder.ts:buildReorderProposal`; `lib/types.ts` for shared proposal types. Pure function. Consumers OH-03, G1.
- **Inputs:** validated `OrderReceipt`, current `Restaurant[]`, current `RevisionedCart`, fresh stable line IDs (caller supplies IDs using `crypto.randomUUID`, making pure tests deterministic). Exactly one source restaurant; UUID sourceOrderId is display context, never ownership proof.
- **Outputs:** `CartProposal {kind:'reorder'|'voice', expectedRevision:number, items:CartItem[], issues:ProposalIssue[], estimatedSubtotalCents:number, sourceOrderId?:string}`. `ProposalIssue {code, lineId?:string, message}`; reorder codes `restaurant_unavailable`, `item_unavailable`, `modifier_unavailable`, `required_choice`, `invalid_quantity`, `invalid_cart`. Any issue blocks Apply. Items have new line IDs, current names/base prices, saved valid group/option IDs/quantities; specialInstructions omitted for reorder. Empty/invalid receipt blocks; max50 lines, quantities1–10. No historic address/tip/promo/totals copied.
- **Pre/post:** source receipt fetched through guest API, current catalog loaded. Function writes nothing and does not mutate inputs. Price comparison uses receipt saved unitPrice versus current configured unit amount; preview labels estimated item subtotal, not authoritative checkout total.
- **Error / retry / concurrency:** malformed inputs produce invalid_cart rather than throw through UI; missing/unavailable choices are shown with line-specific reasons, not dropped/substituted. No partial Apply. Refresh/rebuild is explicit; regenerate IDs only for a new proposal, never on each render/retry.
- **Security / compatibility:** no profile-based ownership, no fixture imports, no special instructions/PII telemetry. Client-only additive type; existing server schemas unchanged.
- **Fixture / freeze / verification:** OH-02 **CREATE** `tests/fixtures/features/reorder.json` with valid, price change, removed option/item, closed restaurant, same-ID note removal, bounds. Freeze at OH-02 pure tests; OH-03 tests consume same fixture. G1 proves original receipt stays exact.

#### FA — Reviewed proposal application and conflict recovery

- **Provider / source / type:** OH-03; **CREATE** `lib/cart-proposal.ts` and `app/components/CartProposalReview.tsx`; reuse `lib/api.ts:saveRevisionedCart`, `fetchRevisionedCart`, `loadCheckoutRecovery`. UI/function contract. Consumers VO-03, G1, G3.
- **Inputs:** issue-free FP-compatible proposal, current selected catalog, current accepted basket, API mode, explicit Apply/Cancel. Voice append/remove/clear proposals use the same complete-basket format. Nonempty basket replacement needs a named confirmation showing current and proposed counts/restaurant.
- **Outputs:** visible states `review`, `applying`, `accepted`, `conflict`, `uncertain`, `error`; accepted output is exact `RevisionedCart` from API. Common callback returns accepted basket, never proposed success. Apply invokes one PUT `{expected_revision,items}`; no preliminary DELETE and no order POST. Cancel returns to originating UI with no write.
- **Pre/post:** proposal valid; pending checkout recovery absent and storage readable. Pending/malformed/unreadable checkout recovery blocks change and links to existing checkout recovery. Session error invalidates proposal. Cart only marked saved after positive PUT or refetch positively matches proposed stable IDs and full canonical contents; provisional subtotal never replaces checkout quote.
- **Errors / retry / ordering:** 409 uses returned currentCart, displays attempted/current changes and requires explicit rebuild/review at new revision. No automatic overwrite/retry. Network/502/504 result is uncertain: refetch basket; exact matching stable IDs/current catalog canonical fields resolves acceptance, otherwise show current basket and require new review. Unavailable read keeps uncertain and Apply blocked. UI suppresses repeated clicks while request/read pending. No persisted proposal required: reload discards intent and fetches current server basket. Catalog changed at save: display returned current prices; user reviews fresh checkout quote before manual order; invalid new choice leaves old basket unchanged.
- **Security / lifecycle:** signed guest via adapter, no chosen owner, no local write presented as durable success, no recovery key clearing. API only; preview disables these feature mutations. Additive frontend contract, existing backend CAS remains authority.
- **Fixture / freeze / verification:** OH-03 **CREATE** `tests/fixtures/features/cart-proposal.json`: acceptance, 409, lost response accepted, failed save unchanged, checkout recovery block. Freeze after unit/real API tests. VO-03 reuses fixture and callbacks; G1/G3 verify writes and isolation.

#### FD — Canonical discovery URL and selection

- **Provider / source / type:** DS-01; **CREATE** `lib/discovery.ts`; `lib/routes.ts`; `lib/marketplace.ts` delegates compatible legacy helpers. Pure selector + URL contract. Consumers DS-02, DS-03, G2.
- **Inputs:** supplied current `Restaurant[]`; URL fields `query` string ≤100 normalized characters; `filter` repeated known labels; `sort` enum recommended/rating/eta/fee/distance; legacy mode normalized to delivery. Default query'', filter[], sort recommended. “All pizza/All restaurants” normalize to no restriction; unknown filters ignored and invalid sort defaults recommended.
- **Outputs:** normalized `DiscoveryQuery {query:string,filters:string[],sort:RestaurantSort}` and matching Restaurant[] plus `matchedMenuItemIds:Record<restaurantId,string[]>`. Filter labels come from existing cuisine/quick filter lists excluding All labels. Combined active filters are AND; each label is independently removable. Search accent/case insensitive normalized substring across restaurant name/cuisine/tags and menu name/description/category; no fuzzy ranking. Matching unavailable dishes may be visible as unavailable, never a valid add action.
- **Pre/post:** canonical supplied catalog; no HTTP/storage writes. Sort copies input; deterministic tie-break restaurant.id lexicographically. Recommended open-first/rating-desc/id; rating desc/id; fee asc/id; eta first numeric lower-bound asc/id, missing last; distance numeric asc/id, missing last. Query trim/accent normalization; URL builders safely encode reserved characters. Long query truncates to100 consistently and UI shows limit.
- **Errors / retry / lifecycle:** malformed URL sanitizes to safe defaults, never crashes; server catalog errors stay errors in DS-02. Old single `filter=Top+Rated` maps case-insensitively to known label; old pickup no longer suggests real pickup. Existing backend `/v1/restaurants` query/sorts unchanged and not used by this new selector; do not mix server filtering and client filtering accidentally.
- **Security / compatibility:** no location collection, no fixture fallback, no user-dependent personalization; old function signatures delegate FD semantics, mapped legacy filters. URL state is additive, no migration.
- **Fixture / freeze / verification:** DS-01 **CREATE** `tests/fixtures/features/discovery.json` with ties, accents, duplicate dish names, tags, unavailable items, malformed/legacy URLs. Freeze with **CREATE** `tests/discovery.test.ts`; DS-02/DS-03 consume fixture and URL builder. G2 browser validates reload/back.

#### FM — Searchable restaurant menu

- **Provider / source / type:** DS-03; `app/restaurants/[restaurantId]/page.tsx`; **CREATE** `lib/menu-search.ts`. Pure menu selector + UI state. Consumers VO-03, G2.
- **Inputs:** current fetched Restaurant, `menuQuery`≤100 characters, selected category ID or All. Unknown category→All. Restaurant-list query propagated as menuQuery only when following a matching-dish link; direct links without it show complete menu.
- **Outputs:** visible categories/item IDs deduped by menuItemId, preserving category/item source order; optional matched query text, selected category, counts, empty/error states. Search item name/description and category name using FD normalization. Unavailable items visible but actions disabled; required modifiers remain on existing item customization page.
- **Pre/post / errors / retry:** read only; no auto-add and no cart changes. Category with zero matching items is omitted except selected category's explicit empty state. Clear search restores all. API errors and empty menu are distinct; retry uses same restaurant/query. Sanitized URLs, refresh/back behavior use FD.
- **Security / concurrency / compatibility:** catalog only from adapter; abort stale fetches/ignore old route response; no unsafe HTML highlight. New query params compatible with existing restaurant path; no schema change.
- **Fixture / freeze / verification:** DS-03 extends synthetic discovery fixture with category/duplicate/unavailable cases and **CREATE** `tests/menu-search.test.ts`. Freeze after selector/browser conformance; VO-03 consumes current Restaurant context, independent of which items are filtered onscreen.

#### FV — Catalog-grounded voice interpretation

- **Provider / source / type:** VO-01; existing `lib/voice.ts`, additive types in `lib/types.ts`. Pure `parseVoiceIntent(transcript,restaurant,currentCart)` result; all consumers must supply context. Consumers VO-03, G3.
- **Inputs:** editable final transcript ≤500 characters; selected current Restaurant, current accepted basket, and caller-supplied fresh stable newLineId for add proposals. Normalized en-US command phrases, quantity digits/one–ten, optional group option names from this menu. No imported mock catalog. One item per add command; an explicit different restaurant, multiple add targets, unrecognized modifier/quantity or unsupported order/pay command yields clarification, never silent default.
- **Outputs:** discriminated result `navigation {target:'cart'}`, `proposal {action:'add'|'remove'|'clear',items:CartItem[],issues:ProposalIssue[]}`, `clarification {code,message,candidateItemIds?:string[],candidateLineIds?:string[]}`, or `unsupported {message}`. App does not retain transcript in result after reset. Exact phrase/token matching to normalized catalog labels; ambiguity returns all matching canonical candidate IDs within selected menu, bounded50. If a restaurant name is spoken it must agree with selected restaurant; otherwise clarify/select manually. Descriptive transcript text is not inserted as special instructions.
- **Pre/post:** context fetched before parse; add uses the supplied stable newLineId from coordinator, not parser randomness; parser returns a complete next-basket proposal whose current line IDs are retained. Same-restaurant add appends one new line without hidden merge; different current-cart restaurant requires explicit replacement via FA. Quantity1–10/lines≤50; no auto defaults for missing required groups unless valid catalog default exists and is displayed for review. Optional groups default empty. Remove resolves a specified existing line; multiple matching lines require choice; clear always reviewed. Negation/cancel phrases and mixed destructive/add instructions produce clarification. No “yes” command applies a proposal.
- **Errors / retry / security:** low confidence/speech text is untrusted input, not permission. No number/currency from transcript controls price. Unsupported command returns typed fallback help, not a speculative match. Zero effects during interpretation; all write authorization passes FA; no /orders POST.
- **Lifecycle / fixture / freeze:** replace unused legacy fixture-first helpers together with existing voice tests; no active application callers rely on old parser. VO-01 **CREATE** `tests/fixtures/features/voice.json`: unique/ambiguous/different-restaurant/negation/injection/quantity/modifier/clear/checkout phrases. Freeze at VO-01 pure test pass and schema match with FP/FA. G3 uses same fixture; manual correction is always possible.

#### FS — Deliberate microphone/text input

- **Provider / source / type:** VO-02; **CREATE** `lib/speech.ts`, `app/components/VoiceInput.tsx`; uses `lib/env.ts` existing browser/mock setting. Browser lifecycle/UI contract. Consumers VO-03, G3.
- **Inputs:** enabled selected-menu panel, explicit Start/Stop/Cancel clicks, browser/mock mode, editable text. Constructor feature detection `SpeechRecognition` or `webkitSpeechRecognition`; missing support offers text. Mock mode never requests microphone, and browser mode never silently emits mocked speech.
- **Outputs:** states idle/listening/stopping/ready/error/unsupported, final editable text and bounded public error kind. Only final results update ready text; interim text labeled provisional and cannot generate apply. UI offers Interpret separately; there is no cart callback in the microphone component.
- **Pre/post / lifecycle:** HTTPS public origin (localhost dev exception), visible privacy notice accepted before Start, no auto-start on mount. `lang='en-US'`, continuous=false, interimResults=true, maxAlternatives=1. Capture session max15 seconds: request stop, then abort after2 seconds if no end; unmount/navigation/page hidden/cancel abort and clear timer, detach listeners, bump generation to ignore late result. No automatic restart. Start rejected/double start returns visible state without crashing.
- **Errors / retry / security:** permission denied, no-speech, network/audio-capture/unavailable→typed text fallback and explicit Retry; no transcript in logs. No app-side raw audio capture/upload/store; browser recognition may send speech to its own remote service. No offline or on-device guarantee. This is disclosed before microphone start, not hidden in developer docs.
- **Versioning / fixture / freeze:** feature detection rather than assumed availability. VO-02 **CREATE** `tests/speech.test.ts` fake recognizer with start/stop/abort/error/end/late events. Freeze after lifecycle test pass. Human real-mic HTTPS test required at G3; mocks cannot prove speech recognition.
- **Verification sources:** [MDN SpeechRecognition](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SpeechRecognition) documents limited availability and possible server-based recognition; [MDN stop](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SpeechRecognition/stop) versus [abort](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SpeechRecognition/abort) distinguish final result from cancellation. Checked October8,2026. These browser capabilities can change; refresh support when implementing.

#### Feature integration gate contracts FG1, FG2, FG3

**Type/provider/consumers:** criterion-indexed exact-build acceptance artifact; G1→DS-01/DS-02/DS-03; G2→VO-01/VO-02/VO-03; G3→future release operator/user. Source: **CREATE** `docs/qa/features/phase-1.md`, `phase-2.md`, `phase-3.md` respectively, owned only by corresponding checkpoint. Inputs all provider tests + actual integrated candidate + synthetic owned fixtures. Outputs source SHA/build/environment/timezone, each numbered criterion's PASS/FAIL/blocked/not-run and evidence, limitations/deferred stabilization pointer. Preconditions consumed contracts frozen and provider code integrated; postcondition only verified phase permits next phase implementation. Failed gate gives reproducible owning-task defect and requires new-build retest. No retry of destructive checkout under a new key. Read-only synthetic screenshots/probes redact guest cookies/transcripts/addresses. Compatible report format, no schema migration. Fixture is the corresponding phase journey described in §17.11. Freeze occurs only at checkpoint acceptance; relevant code changes invalidate affected evidence. Verification checks artifact fields and all required scenario results; no mocked microphone pass.

### 17.8 Workstreams and execution waves

| Wave | Workstream / tasks | Start condition | Merge order and write ownership |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | History OH-01; reorder resolver OH-02 | baseline facts rechecked; existing APIs understood | OH-01 then OH-02; disjoint files, both can be designed concurrently |
| W2 | Reviewed mutation OH-03 | FH/FP fixtures frozen | after OH-01/OH-02; owns history/receipt wiring, proposal component and CSS |
| W3 | G1 | OH-01–03 integrated | evidence first, coordinator updates statuses last |
| W4 | Discovery DS-01 | G1 verified | owns shared routes/types/selectors; no parallel writers |
| W5 | Discovery UI DS-02 | FD frozen | owns homepage/list/CSS; merge before DS-03 |
| W6 | Menu DS-03 | FD frozen; DS-02 merged | owns menu page, menu selector, routes additions and CSS; serialized due shared files |
| W7 | G2 | DS-01–03 integrated | evidence/coordinator only |
| W8 | Parser VO-01; recognition VO-02 | G2 verified; browser-default assumption reconfirmed | independent lib files; VO-01 owns types, VO-02 owns env/speech/input; merge VO-01 then VO-02 |
| W9 | Voice coordinator VO-03 | FV/FS/FA/FM frozen and providers merged | owns new voice panel and menu insertion/CSS; providers' shared API/types changes require owner review |
| W10 | G3 | all phases integrated | full regression, real microphone, evidence and docs; no app source changes in QA packet |

This is a safe concurrency map, not an instruction to create agents. Implement serially by default. Only coordinator updates this guide, CI configuration or checkpoint reports; behavior owners append their own test files. No two same-wave packets own the same file. If fixes require an earlier owner's file, route back to that task, then retest dependents.

#### OH-01 — Make guest history browseable beyond the first page

**Status:** Not completed / queued. **Objective:** Load owned receipts in pages of20, keep useful history visible on a later-page fault, and explain browser-scoped retention.

**Why this task exists:** Owns this single user-visible capability or cross-component acceptance outcome, with its tests in the same packet. **Workstream / execution wave / owner:** History, W1; future implementer in this repository.

**Depends on:** None among new tickets; rechecked existing canonical guest/catalog/cart/receipt baseline. **Blocks / consumers:** OH-03 via FH; G1 via FH.

**Inputs:** FH records in §17.6, their synthetic provider fixtures, rechecked source paths in §17.2 and FADR decisions. Baseline consumes current supplied Restaurant/cart, signed guest API and immutable receipt schema; no profile ID or local cached order is an ownership input.

**Outputs / contracts produced:** FH; the exact output shape/error/retry/version rules are in §17.6. **Contracts consumed:** FH; consume only documented public fields/fixtures, not provider internals.

**Owned files:**

- `app/orders/page.tsx` — existing; scoped responsibility described in steps.
- `tests/api.test.ts` — existing; scoped responsibility described in steps.
- **CREATE** `lib/history.ts` — behavior/fixture/evidence owned by this packet.
- **CREATE** `tests/history.test.ts` — behavior/fixture/evidence owned by this packet.
- **CREATE** `tests/fixtures/features/history.json` — behavior/fixture/evidence owned by this packet.
- **CREATE** `e2e/history-reorder.spec.ts` — behavior/fixture/evidence owned by this packet.

**Non-owned / do-not-touch:** all files outside the owned list, especially `backend/app/main.py`, `backend/app/store.py`, `backend/app/catalog.py`, `backend/app/order_service.py`, `backend/migrations/`, `app/checkout/page.tsx`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `infra/render.yaml`, unrelated audit/graph artifacts and provider settings. Coordinator alone maintains shared guide/phase statuses. No dependency/framework additions assumed.

**Worked verification for a new implementer — OH-01**

- **Arrange:** Create21 owned receipts with deterministic ordering plus a second guest; use the existing fetchOrderReceipts adapter.
- **Act and assert the accepted path:** Load20, request the next page using the last returned ID, and display the final receipt exactly once. Fail the second-page request and retain the first20 with Retry.
- **Act and assert the failure path:** Reset the session while a page is in flight and resolve the old request last. No old guest rows return; a foreign cursor cannot disclose another guest history.
- **Proof and handoff:** Put these scenarios in this packet's owned tests/evidence. Run its exact verification commands, record expected versus actual response and durable state, and map results to the numbered criteria. Follow section0 for setup, redaction and contract handoff. This added walkthrough is NOT RUN and does not change the packet's recorded status.

**Implementation steps / TODOs:**

- [ ] **OH-01.01** — Use existing fetchOrderReceipts({limit:20,cursor,signal}) and last returned ID; never invent a separate history API.
- [ ] **OH-01.02** — Keep initial/loading/loading-more/empty/error states separate; dedupe by ID and disable repeated Load more while in flight.
- [ ] **OH-01.03** — Abort/ignore obsolete responses, reset rows and cursors on guest/session reset; add explicit Refresh that starts first page.
- [ ] **OH-01.04** — Show saved date, quantity, mock Placed status and saved total, with exact receipt links; no fabricated historical restaurant name.
- [ ] **OH-01.05** — Document current-browser expiry limitation; retain local_demo unavailable behavior.
- [ ] **OH-01.06** — Create FH fixture and unit/adapter/browser cases, including21 orders and foreign cursor.

**Invariants affected:** FINV-01,08,12; preserve stated enforcement and add the packet-specific negative cases. **Failure/error semantics:** Show typed network/session/cursor errors; no cache fallback; preserve prior rows only within the same active guest.

**Security/privacy:** use guest-derived authorization and canonical IDs; no fixture outage fallback, transcript/audio/PII/credentials in logs/storage/artifacts; synthetic QA inputs only. Review retained screenshots/logs for private values. No direct order submission except existing manual checkout.

**Observability:** existing typed errors and request IDs plus dated acceptance observations. Expose meaningful loading/validation/conflict/error state; assert these through tests. Do not add analytics or log raw user text.

**Migration/backfill/compatibility:** N/A for database migration—additive frontend behavior on unchanged guest/cart/receipt API. Existing preview/guest expiry/mock payment behavior preserved. Update all known consumer tests together if a frozen client interface changes; existing backend response schema remains version1.

**Required tests:** Unit page cursor/dedupe/late-response/error states; adapter limit/cursor/signal tests; real21-order PG API journey and second guest; existing guest-profile/receipt regression. Behavior-level tests include numbered acceptance cases. Backend integration required where mutation/isolation is involved; otherwise BACKEND remains checkpoint regression. Microphone mocks prove lifecycle only.

**Verification commands:** definitions/prerequisites in §17.2 apply; future CREATE tests must exist first. Do not claim a test file passed before it exists.

```sh
npm run test -- tests/history.test.ts tests/api.test.ts
npm run test:web
npm run test:e2e:list
```

**Acceptance criteria:**

1. **OH-01-AC1 — PASS/FAIL:** Twenty receipts display first; Load more retrieves remaining owned IDs in server order with no duplicates.
2. **OH-01-AC2 — PASS/FAIL:** A failed next page preserves loaded rows and offers Retry; empty success is distinct from API fault.
3. **OH-01-AC3 — PASS/FAIL:** Foreign cursor/receipt never leaks data and session reset clears old display; preview stays unavailable.

**Rollback/recovery:** Revert this feature diff to last verified source, rebuild, and refetch current server state; never restore a stale client basket or delete accepted receipts. Cancel/discard ephemeral draft; retain existing checkout recovery.

### 17.11 Integration checkpoints

**G1:** On isolated actual PG/API/Next candidate, create21+ owned synthetic receipts and a second guest. Load first20 then remaining; a foreign cursor/order must fail. Reopen old receipt, edit live menu price, reorder into review with old/new amounts, cancel (zero write), then replace existing basket using one PUT. Verify new line IDs/current canonical prices, old receipt byte-equivalent, same-restaurant and cross-restaurant replacement confirmation. Removed dish/modifier/closed restaurant blocks all-or-nothing Apply. Race another same-guest tab and lose a success response; show accepted/current basket without silent reapply. An uncertain checkout recovery record blocks proposal; session reset removes access; local_demo never exposes reorder/history. Run manual checkout only afterward, new key/new receipt, not from reorder. Exit: all G1 numbered criteria and affected source tests pass on one SHA.

**G2:** Enter query+two filters+sort; each navigation/search/sidebar action preserves others, refresh/back/forward restores exact visible state. Old links normalize predictably; sort ties stable. Search a dish found only in API-edited catalog, open the correct menu with matching query, choose category, clear search and customize item with existing cart behavior. API error remains visible, closed/unavailable items disabled, no pickup claim, no location-dependent inference. Run 375px and keyboard path. Preview discovery remains labeled and API-free. Exit: all G2 criteria pass and G1 regression stays green on integrated build.

**G3 / final feature gate:** Execute typed and fake-recognizer add/modifier/quantity, ambiguous item, clear, specific remove, cancel, corrected transcript, unsupported checkout command; every mutation uses reviewed FA and never /orders directly. Human test with actual microphone on HTTPS in current supported desktop browser (record browser/OS/language) and one available mobile browser (record supported or fallback); unsupported browser, denied permission, no speech, network fault and navigation cleanup have safe typed path. Synthetic recognizer tests verify cleanup/timeouts; real speech checks prove audible phrases become editable text and proposed correct IDs. Repeat all phase journeys, current seven CI gates, public guest receipt/isolation smoke and preview guards on same build. Exit: all G3 criteria and human check recorded; missing device/access leaves that target blocked, not accepted. Deferred ST-13 stays deferred.

### 17.13 Critical path and parallelization plan

Critical path: `OH-02 → OH-03 → G1 → DS-01 → DS-02 → DS-03 → G2 → max(VO-01,VO-02) → VO-03 → G3`; OH-01 joins before OH-03. Phase order is user-chosen, so Discovery and Voice implementation wait for earlier acceptance even when code could technically be designed earlier. Contract draft preparation can occur before runtime providers, but merge waits for fixtures + conformance. DS-02/DS-03 remain serialized because they touch shared routes/styles. No parallel changes to lib/types, lib/api, menu page, CSS or guide without explicit owner handoff. Real microphone/device access may dominate final waiting time; it does not prevent Phase1 work.

### 17.14 Release, migration, rollback, and observability gates

1. **Before each implementation packet:** refresh main/review working tree; verify source facts and paths; preserve untracked QA/graph files; check consumed fixture freeze. Start with **OH-01**, then OH-02. Implementation approval is separate from this planning request.
2. **Before each merge:** relevant unit/browser contract checks + WEB; existing seven CI gates and both API/preview suites must pass on candidate. No test deletion/skipping to get green. Separate future publish/merge/deploy authority from local verification.
3. **Migration:** N/A—current plan is additive frontend behavior; no DB schema or backfill. Before implementation verify current APIs still support assumed fields. If a new requirement needs schema change, add explicit owner/forward/mixed-version/rollback packet first. Never edit applied migration checksums.
4. **Rollout:** Phase1 then2 then3; release operator can deploy each accepted slice. Existing NEXT_PUBLIC_VOICE_MODE=mock supports typed/mock deterministic testing; browser mode is enabled for real microphone validation deliberately and requires rebuild. No app-paid provider secrets or new infrastructure. Keep production synthetic boundaries and the existing readiness proof.
5. **Rollback:** revert the affected feature commits to last accepted source, rebuild/redeploy through existing process, fetch current server basket/receipt and repeat smoke. No database rollback/delete needed. Client proposals discarded; existing backend data remains source of truth. If a guest legitimately changed basket before rollback, do not restore old basket over it.
6. **Observability:** use existing typed errors/request IDs and per-criterion QA records. No new analytics service/always-running monitor. Logs contain coarse state/error code only if needed; never transcript/audio/receipt contents/addresses/guest token. Existing telemetry helper accepts arbitrary properties: do not pass raw transcript or error/provider content. Useful QA observations: page error vs empty, stale revision, proposed vs accepted price, recognizer exit/cancellation; no fabricated dashboard claims.
7. **Final feature release acceptance:** G3 current source/build/CI identity, actual public access/current guest receipt isolation, original checkout regression, manual mic+fallback record, docs consistent with limitations. The deferred stabilization acceptance ledger is a separate open obligation and cannot be marked Complete by this gate.

| Remote graph indexing denied | Automatic review rejected possible private-source export. | Local inspection completed plan; optional indexing is unavailable, not a feature blocker. |

No credentials, real customer data or new paid provider needed for Phase1/2. Runtime access and real microphone/device checks become true acceptance blockers only when that target is being verified. API contract drift discovered after refresh is an execution blocker until the affected packet is revised. Ordinary coding/testing work is not a blocker.

### 18.1 Project charter

**Goal:** a connected sales demo that can support the first paid local Indian restaurant. Guests order dine-in/takeaway and pay at restaurant; staff progress orders and record full payments; owners manage menu/hours/tables/staff and explicitly approve SMS/email campaigns; voice proposes changes for review. Public demo remains synthetic with no external sends or money movement.

**Current:** guest-scoped mock ordering, canonical catalog, revisioned cart and idempotent immutable mock receipts exist. Staff authorization, restaurant-owned business history, real campaign work and catalog-grounded browser voice are not implemented in the inspected branch. **Desired:** all four user-required capabilities in one complete first release, with code/review/runtime evidence distinguished.

**Why now:** the plan is approved, but previous T1/T3/T6 tasks span multiple days and hidden contracts. The work exists to make implementation delegable, not to claim demand. No restaurant has yet agreed to pay. Success means the named G1–G8/E1–E5 criteria pass on a named build and real pilot evidence is obtained; no fabricated revenue or latency target.

**Non-goals:** online payment collection, delivery, aggregator data/access, international tax platform, shared tabs, split/partial bills, scheduled pickup, stock/payroll/accounting, autonomous speech submission or automatic marketing decisions. No new queue/cache/LLM platform. Retain existing mock release obligations independently.

| I05 | Operational completion is independent of recorded payment and reversal | Separate append-only events; locked order version | RS-21, RS-22, RS-23, RS-38, RS-49 | G3 races and paid-cancelled settlement |
| I06 | QR/demo profile is not staff authority; revoked membership fails next action | Verified Clerk subject, DB membership and explicit demo scope | RS-04, RS-05, RS-06, RS-08, RS-58 | G2 role matrix and G7 forged demo test |
| I07 | Campaign sends use frozen approval, bounded spend and no uncertain resend | SQL recipient reservation, suppression recheck and reconciliation | RS-29, RS-30, RS-33, RS-34, RS-35, RS-36, RS-37 | G6 two-worker cap race/crash/callback tests |
| I08 | Consent is explicit per restaurant/channel; secrets and contacts do not leak | Separate consent/suppression rows, secret aliases, safe logs | RS-24, RS-25, RS-26, RS-30, RS-60, RS-63 | G6 opt-out race and redaction checks |
| I09 | Unknown live configuration or dependency outage cannot become synthetic success | Disabled defaults, readiness gates and explicit activation | RS-11, RS-30, RS-60, RS-61, RS-65, RS-67 | G7/G8 configuration and outage tests |
| I10 | Theme/layout/voice cannot lose draft state or confirm a command | Stable state owner, reviewed proposals, accessible native controls | RS-39 through RS-57 | E1–E5 and G5 keyboard/voice/browser checks |
